$comment: Advisory rubric scores (evals/rubric.md), given by Claude after looking at each output at 390 and 1280 px. Self-scores run high, so they never pass a gate; they help the designer review. Dimensions: hierarchy, brandFit, readability, facts, standard, phone. Evidence is given for every score below 5.

evidence.hierarchy: The opening sentence names all three products, and the list right after it repeats them.

evidence.standard: It ends by offering to draft a purchase order, which the prototype can’t make yet; offers should be limited to what can be made.
It corrects the premise (sales rose) and charts it, but the chart’s short lead doesn’t say why the week before was low.

evidence.brandFit: “Breathable & Easy to Wear” is generic copy, not the store’s voice.
evidence.standard: 57 characters is within the limit, but the second half adds little a shopper searches for.

evidence.readability: Long for a chat reply: a short answer then five bullets; could offer the policy as a document instead.
evidence.facts: The usual return windows and the note on Indian e-commerce rules are general knowledge, not checked against a source.

evidence.phone: At 390 px only every other month is labelled on the axis.

evidence.brandFit: The letterhead shows a dashed “No logo supplied” box: honest (D-61), but it looks unfinished in a demo; the sample store has no logo file.
evidence.standard: No total row under the orders table; a reader has to add up 126 rows.

evidence.brandFit: The letterhead shows the dashed “No logo supplied” box: honest (D-61), but it looks unfinished in a demo.
evidence.phone: At 390 px the page preview is scaled to the screen, so its text is about 5 px; the PDF and Word downloads are the readable form on a phone. This is the existing document card's behaviour (/document-chat), not changed here.
